difficultyReason: The stimulus uses a disjunctive syllogism (A ∨ B; ¬A; ∴ B), which requires the student to formalize the argument before scanning answer choices. Several distractors share surface topic similarity or use a similar conclusion but differ in logical form (e.g., conditional rather than disjunctive structure), making it moderately challenging.
stimulus: The contamination in the reservoir originated either from agricultural runoff or from a malfunctioning treatment facility. Investigators have confirmed that there was no agricultural runoff during the relevant period. Therefore, the contamination must have originated from the malfunctioning treatment facility.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The budget shortfall was caused either by declining tax revenue or by increased municipal spending. Since increased municipal spending has been ruled out by auditors, the shortfall must have been caused by declining tax revenue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the treatment facility malfunctioned, then contamination would enter the reservoir. The facility did malfunction, so contamination must have entered the reservoir.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Agricultural runoff typically causes reservoir contamination. Because there was significant agricultural activity upstream, the reservoir contamination was most likely caused by runoff.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The contamination in the reservoir could not have come from the treatment facility unless the facility had malfunctioned. The facility did not malfunction, so the contamination must have come from somewhere other than the facility.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whenever both agricultural runoff and treatment-facility failures occur simultaneously, reservoir contamination is inevitable. Both events occurred, so the reservoir became contaminated.

explanations.correct: The stimulus has the form: A ∨ B; ¬A; ∴ B (disjunctive syllogism). Choice A matches exactly: either declining tax revenue (A) or increased spending (B) caused the shortfall; increased spending has been ruled out (¬B... wait — ¬B here is 'spending ruled out,' which parallels ¬A in the stimulus); therefore declining tax revenue is responsible (A). The structure is: X ∨ Y; ¬Y; ∴ X — a clean disjunctive syllogism with the same two-premise structure and a necessary conclusion ('must have been').
explanations.A: Correct. Matches the disjunctive syllogism perfectly: two exclusive alternatives, one is eliminated, therefore the other must be the cause. The conclusion's modal force ('must have been') also matches the stimulus.
explanations.B: Wrong structure. This is modus ponens (If P then Q; P; ∴ Q), not a disjunctive syllogism. It introduces a conditional premise that does not appear in the stimulus.
explanations.C: Wrong structure and wrong strength. This uses an analogical/probabilistic inference from general tendencies ('typically causes') to a 'most likely' conclusion. The stimulus has two exhaustive alternatives and reaches a necessary conclusion, not a probabilistic one.
explanations.D: Wrong structure. This is modus tollens (A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A), applied to a conditional derived from the disjunct. It also reaches a weaker, open-ended conclusion ('somewhere other than the facility') rather than identifying a specific positive cause.
explanations.E: Wrong structure. This is a conjunctive sufficient condition (A ∧ B → C; A ∧ B; ∴ C) — modus ponens with a conjunctive antecedent. There is no disjunction and no elimination of alternatives.
